answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to complete a verifiable sequence of modular squarings, with every result depending on the previous one. GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot reduce the elapsed time of a single chain by parallelizing its steps. Simulating clones therefore demands additional sequential work and preserves a physical-time bottleneck. A mirror identity offers no shortcut: a velvet signal of valid proofs appears only after the required computation.
